title: Writing Verilog-A for ngspice
intro: Verilog-A describes a device by the currents and voltages on its branches as equations; OpenVAF compiles it to an .osdi file and ngspice solves it like a built-in device. This page teaches the language through three models that were compiled and run here, and lists what OpenVAF's subset leaves out.

items: `include \"disciplines.vams\" (electrical, thermal and other natures) and `include \"constants.vams\" (`P_Q, `P_K, `M_PI ...). OpenVAF has its own copies built in.
module name(port1, port2, ...); with inout and electrical declarations for each port, and extra electrical (or thermal) nodes for internal nodes.
parameter real name = default from (low:high); with the range checked at load time; from [0:inf) includes 0. parameter integer for switches.
analog begin ... end: the equations. Contributions I(a,b) <+ expr add a current from a to b; V(a,b) <+ expr makes the branch a voltage source. Several contributions to one branch add up.

ddt(x) is d/dt (capacitance as ddt(charge)), idt(x, ic) an integral, limexp(x) an exponential with built-in limiting that helps Newton converge, \$temperature the device temperature in kelvin, \$vt the thermal voltage kT/q, \$abstime the transient time.
white_noise(psd, \"name\") and flicker_noise(k, exponent, \"name\") contributions add noise that .noise reports under that name.
Variables with (* desc=\"...\", units=\"...\" *) become operating-point outputs (@n1[name]).

blocks.text: A diode with charge storage and noise

items: The series resistance makes an internal node ai. When rs = 0, the else branch V(a, ai) <+ 0 shorts it, and OpenVAF collapses the node so the matrix stays non-singular.
limexp instead of exp: the simulator may try huge voltages during Newton iterations; limexp grows linearly beyond a point so nothing overflows.

The depletion charge uses the SPICE formula below vj/2 and a linear extension above it, so the charge stays finite in forward bias. A Verilog-A model must be continuous and smooth everywhere the simulator might go, not just in the intended region.
The previous page's testbench compares it with the built-in diode: same operating point and the same noise.

blocks.text: A thermal node: a self-heating resistor

blocks.source:
Self-heating resistor: 5 V applied at t = 0, resistance rises as it heats
V1 a 0 DC 0 PWL(0 0 1m 5 3 5)
N1 a 0 sh
.model sh shres r0=100 tc1=4e-3 rth=500 cth=1e-3
.control
  pre_osdi shres.osdi
  save all @n1[trise]
  tran 1m 3
  meas tran i_on  find i(V1) at=2m
  meas tran i_end find i(V1) at=3
  meas tran trise find @n1[trise] at=3
  let r_on = -5/i_on
  let r_end = -5/i_end
  print r_on r_end
.endc
.end

blocks.text: The thermal node dt carries power (Pwr) as its flow and temperature (Temp) as its potential, so the electrical power is a current source into a thermal resistor and capacitor. In steady state R = 100 (1 + 0.004 x 500 x 25/R), so R^2 - 100 R - 5000 = 0 and R = 136.6 ohms with a 91.5 K rise; the run reaches both after a few thermal time constants (Rth Cth = 0.5 s).

blocks.source:
Verilog-A integrator driven by a 1 V step
V1 i 0 DC 0 PWL(0 0 1u 1)
N1 i o imod
.model imod integ k=1k
R1 o 0 1k
.control
  pre_osdi integ.osdi
  tran 1u 1m
  meas tran v1m find v(o) at=1m
.endc
.end

blocks.text: k = 1000 per second integrates 1 V for 1 ms to 1 V (0.9995 V, since the step takes 1 us). Behavioural Verilog-A like this is handy, but the analog-only, compact-model subset that OpenVAF accepts limits it, as the next section shows.
What OpenVAF and ngspice do not support
OpenVAF compiles the compact-modelling subset of Verilog-AMS (LRM 2.4). Tested here with OpenVAF-Reloaded and ngspice 47:

items: Works: ddt, idt, ddx (partial derivatives), limexp, \$abstime, \$temperature, \$vt, \$simparam, analysis(), \$bound_step, @(initial_step) and @(final_step) with \$strobe or \$display, white_noise, flicker_noise, analog functions, branches, internal nodes, thermal and other disciplines.

Rejected by the compiler: transition(), slew(), laplace_* and zi_* filters, and event controls other than initial_step and final_step (no @(cross(...)) or @(timer(...))). Digital and mixed-signal Verilog-AMS (always, logic, wreal) is out of scope.
Compiles but fails in ngspice: absdelay() (the operating point fails with timestep too small).

So for behavioural system models, combine: Verilog-A for smooth device equations, XSPICE code models for delays, slew limits and digital behaviour, and B sources for quick expressions. Simulators like Xyce or Spectre run the wider Verilog-A language.
Compile errors point to the line; openvaf-r --print-expansion shows the source after macros and includes.
\$strobe(\"vd=%g\", vd) inside @(final_step) or unconditionally prints values (every iteration, so keep it short).

Compare against a known model at a few operating points (as the diode testbench does), and sweep far outside the normal range to find discontinuities: a dc sweep from -100 V to +100 V with deriv() of the current shows jumps in conductance that will break Newton later.
A singular matrix at an internal node (check node n1#ai) means a node with no defined current path: add a contribution or collapse it.

blocks.title: Capacitor
blocks.text: Write the analog block of a linear capacitor c between ports p and n, and of a nonlinear one with C(V) = c0 (1 + a V).
solution: Nonlinear: write the charge, Q(V) = c0 (V + a V^2 / 2), so that dQ/dV = C(V): I(p,n) <+ ddt(c0 * (V(p,n) + a*V(p,n)*V(p,n)/2)); This conserves charge, unlike multiplying C(V) by ddt(V).
blocks.answer: I(p,n) <+ ddt(Q(V)) with Q the integral of C(V).
